title: Lifting and preserving state

sources.locator: React Learn and Reference; React 19.2; provisions applicable to Lifting and preserving state
sources.claim: Shared state moves to the nearest common owner, which passes values and callbacks to coordinated children.

canonicalExplanation.summary: When two components must show the **same** changing value, don't give each its own copy and try to sync them. **Lift** the state to their **nearest common parent**, which owns one value and passes it down with callbacks. Each child becomes a controlled view of that one source. The flip side: React **keeps** a component's state as long as the same component stays at the same place in the tree. To **reset** it on purpose, for example a form when you switch to another lesson, give it a different **key**.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A science lesson has a Celsius box and a Fahrenheit box. Each keeps its own state and calls the other through callbacks to stay in sync; typing fast leaves them showing 100°C and 50°F. Two temperature inputs share one converted value owned by their common calculator parent. In this lesson you'll repair unsynchronized sibling state and control when form state resets.

```predict
{"question": "Siblings A and B both need `temperature`. Where should the state live?", "options": ["In A, copied into B", "In their nearest common parent, passed to both"], "answer": 1, "why": "One owner means one truth. Children receive the value and a callback."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **Props and composition** module, **Event propagation and delegation**, **Minimal and normalized state** (no duplicates), and **Lists and stable keys**, since keys also control state reset.

examples.title: Two temperature boxes, one truth
examples.situation: Two temperature inputs share one converted value owned by their common calculator parent.
walkthrough: **Problem:** each input had its own state and synced through callbacks, so fast typing left them disagreeing.
**Lift:** Calculator owns one { scale, text } value, and the other box is derived by converting it.
**Test:** type 100 in Celsius and a test will see 212 in Fahrenheit; type 32 in Fahrenheit and see 0 in Celsius.
examples.result: The two boxes always agree, because one converted value is owned by their common parent.

examples.title: The draft that followed you
examples.situation: A lesson page renders `<NoteForm />` in the same spot for every lesson. Learners switching lessons see the previous lesson's unsaved note.
walkthrough: Same component in the same position, so React kept its state.
The form should belong to one lesson.
examples.result: Each lesson starts with an empty note form, and nothing leaks between lessons.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Duplicating shared state in both children is safe if callbacks try to keep it synchronized.
misconceptions.correction: Two copies can fall out of sync through timing, missed paths or bugs. Lift the state to one owner so there's only one value to be right.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "Two temperature boxes, one truth", why did the boxes disagree?

analogy.example: Two children each keeping their own copy of the family calendar will soon disagree. Put **one calendar on the fridge** (the common parent); everyone reads it and asks the parent to add events. A **key** is like **a new calendar for a new year**: same fridge spot, fresh pages.
limitations: Calendars don't auto-convert units; derived values do.
Moving the calendar to another room is like changing position: state may reset.

steps.explanation: The common calculator parent owns one value.
Typing 212 in Fahrenheit updates the shared value with its scale.
Both inputs share one converted value, so they agree.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing a lifted temperature. Step 1, Owner: temp is { scale: c, text: 20 }; fahrenheit (derived) is 68. The common calculator parent owns one value. Step 2, Edit: temp is { scale: f, text: 212 }. Typing 212 in Fahrenheit updates the shared value with its scale. Step 3, Render: Celsius box is 100; Fahrenheit box is 212. Both inputs share one converted value, so they agree.

nearTransfer.prompt: A filter bar and a results list are siblings. Lift `query` into their parent Page, pass it to both, and give the bar an onQueryChange callback.

farTransfer.prompt: Build a tabbed editor where each tab has its own draft that should survive switching tabs, plus a "New document" button that starts fresh. Decide which state to lift and where to use keys, and test both behaviours.
scaffold: Drafts per tab in the parent.

remediation.explanation: When two components show the same value, ask: **Who's their closest shared parent?** Move the state there. When state sticks around unexpectedly, ask: **Should this be a new instance?** Change its key.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The draft that followed you".

recap.summary: To repair unsynchronized sibling state, lift the shared value to the nearest common parent, derive related values there, and pass values and callbacks to the children. Control when form state resets by keeping the same position to preserve it or changing the key to start fresh.
